data.title: LASE Appoints Dmitri Nikitin Executive Chairman
data.description:
ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / Laser Photonics Corporation , an emerging directed energy and laser technology platform developing applications for defense, semiconductor, pharmaceutical and industrial markets (the "Company"), today announced the appointment of Dmitri Nikitin, the Company's founder, as Executive Chairman of the Board of Directors and principal executive officer responsible for leading the Company, with the authority and responsibilities customarily associated with the Chief Executive Officer role.

The appointment supports the Company's strategy to build on its industrial laser business and expand into higher-value applications in defense and semiconductor markets. Dmitri Nikitin brings more than 35 years of experience in laser technology innovation. He holds an engineering degree in industrial electronics and quantum mechanics from Moscow Power Engineering University and a PHD in Ministry of Electronics of USSR.

His product innovation and executive leadership across multinational companies include the development of laser platforms for marking, cutting, welding, glass separation, flat panel display processing, wafer processing, semiconductor processing and industrial manufacturing. His engineering leadership at the Institute of Precise Technologies in the former Soviet Union helped create new laser applications for components used in the space program.

Mr. Nikitin's inventions include patented methods for splitting precision glass with zero curve loss. He co-developed the world's first high-power fiber laser cutting system for IPG Photonics. Mr. Nikitin developed a mobile fiber-laser platform for military mine-clearing applications, the first of its kind. He is a named inventor on three patent applications in 2026 relating to Bulk-to-Shape technology.

Mr. Nikitin's initial priorities will include advancing the Company's Laser Shield Anti-Drone ("LSAD") platform, strengthening its engineering capabilities, developing a disciplined marketing and sales organization and seamlessly integrating the Company's previous acquisitions and multiple product lines into one coherent organization.

Dmitri Nikitin said, "We see an opportunity to apply our laser technology experience to solving two important challenges: defending against emerging drone threats with affordable and easily deployable directed energy laser systems and, modernizing the U.S. military's domestic manufacturing capacity with our existing industrial laser platforms."

Commenting on his appointment, Qing Lu, Chair of the Company's Audit Committee, said, "We are pleased Mr. Nikitin accepted our proposal to step in and lead our enterprise. His experience developing and scaling applications for large international markets is exactly what our organization needs for the future."

  • Mr. Nikitin will assume the principal executive officer responsibilities previously held by Wayne Tupuola, who resigned as Chief Executive Officer for medical reasons effective October 13, 2026. Mr. Nikitin will perform these responsibilities as Executive Chairman, and the Company does not currently intend to appoint a separate Chief Executive Officer. Ann Tewari's service as interim President concluded on October 13, 2026, and she returned to her previous position as Global Vice President, Operations and Strategy.
  • Companies led by Mr. Nikitin have won numerous honors, including Laser Photonics' IEN Best Brands Award and William C. Schwartz Industry Innovation Award from the Metro Orlando Economic Development Commission. Other honors include Florida's Governor's Business Diversification Award in the Green-to-Gold category.

About Laser Photonics Corporation

Laser Photonics Corporation is an emerging defense and directed energy technology platform focused on developing laser applications to address defense and security needs and applying its core industrial laser products to help modernize the domestic manufacturing infrastructure required to support U.S. national security.

The Company develops laser platforms for four principal markets: defense, semiconductor, pharmaceutical and industrial. Through internal development, strategic acquisitions and partnerships, LASE intends to expand its technology portfolio, strengthen its advanced manufacturing capabilities, scale the enterprise profitably and build shareholder value.

data.title: Kopin to Host Live YouTube "Ask Me Anything" Panel from Nasdaq MarketSite on the Future of AI Infrastructure
data.description:
Kopin Corporation (), a leading provider of application-specific optical systems and high-performance microdisplays for defense, training, enterprise, industrial, consumer and medical products, invites investors, technology professionals, industry observers, and AI enthusiasts to virtually join a YouTube "Ask Me Anything" (AMA) event titled "The Trillion Dollar AI Bottleneck" on October 20, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. EDT, streamed live from Nasdaq MarketSite.

Livestream Access: Live From NYC: The Trillion Dollar AI Bottleneck

Participants are encouraged to virtually join the livestream and submit questions in real time as the panel explores what it will take to build the infrastructure backbone for the AI-driven economy. Questions can also be submitted in advance to events@kopin.com.

The interactive livestream will feature a panel of distinguished thought leaders from across the AI and technology ecosystem:

  • James Altucher, Senior Strategic Advisor, Fabric.AI

  • Cortney Harding, AI and Emerging Technology Expert and Founder, Friends with Holograms

  • Michael Murray, Chief Executive Officer, President and Chairperson, Kopin Corporation

As AI models grow larger and more powerful, demand for compute resources, networking, energy, and data infrastructure continues to rise. During the discussion, panelists will examine the challenges and opportunities shaping the future of AI, including data center capacity, optical interconnect technologies, infrastructure scalability, and the innovations required to sustain AI's rapid expansion.

Unlike a traditional panel discussion, audience participation will play a central role. Viewers will be invited to submit questions live through the YouTube event, helping guide the conversation and providing direct access to the panelists' insights on some of the industry's most pressing topics.

"AI development is moving at extraordinary speed, but the physical infrastructure needed to support that growth presents significant challenges and opportunities," said Michael Murray, CEO, President and Chairperson of Kopin. "This discussion will explore the technologies and investments necessary to overcome these bottlenecks and unlock the next phase of AI innovation."

data.title: Stellantis Faces a New Labor Test in Canada
data.description:
Stellantis NV (STLA, Financials), the automaker behind Jeep, Ram and Chrysler, is facing a new labor test in Canada as more than 9,000 unionized workers prepare to vote on strike authorization this weekend.

The vote is scheduled for Oct. 17 and 18 after contract talks with Unifor stalled.

A strike authorization does not automatically mean workers will walk off the job, but it gives the union more leverage if negotiations continue to drag.

The biggest issues are job security and the future of an assembly plant outside Toronto that currently sits idle.

Stellantis had planned to retool the facility for Jeep Compass production, but later paused that plan and shifted production to Illinois. The company now wants to sell the Canadian plant to a defense contractor.

That makes the dispute about more than wages.

For investors, it adds another execution risk while Stellantis is already trying to reshape its business with a $70 billion turnaround plan and new vehicle architecture.

The company is targeting meaningful cost savings by 2028, so prolonged labor disruption would complicate that effort.

The next thing to watch is the weekend vote and whether it pushes Stellantis and Unifor closer to a deal.

data.title: Wall Street Is Unusually Optimistic About Third-Quarter Earnings. Here's Why in 5 Charts. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Elijah Nicholson-Messmer

While it was a mixed week of earnings reports from the big banks, Wall Street analysts still expect big things to come from the third-quarter earnings season that's now under way.

The S&P 500 is expected to report earnings growth of 29.0% for the third quarter — the third straight period of 25%-plus growth. It's an impressive streak, given that the index's earnings have grown at an?average quarterly clip of 12.6% over the past decade, according to FactSet.

The third-quarter growth is likely to head even higher, once companies start reporting, given the typical history of earnings beats from Corporate America.

Already, a historic number of S&P 500 companies have forecast earnings for the quarter above what analysts had expected. Wall Street, in other words, is full of good vibes.

Here are five charts that show how this corporate confidence is breaking out across the index — and where it might be heading.

The 72 companies offering upbeat forecasts is unprecedented, according to FactSet.

"This quarter marks the highest number of S&P 500 companies issuing positive EPS guidance for a quarter since FactSet began tracking this metric in 2006," FactSet Senior Earnings Analyst John Butters wrote in a recent note.

On the other side of things, just 44 companies have offered downbeat guidance — well below the 10-year average of 57.

Stocks in the information technology sector have dominated the strong guidance. The sector accounts for 44 of the 72 total positive preannouncements.

Within tech, software and semiconductor companies are leading the charge. Fueled by seemingly insatiable demand for artificial intelligence, the semiconductor industry alone is projected to grow Q3 earnings by 130% year-over-year.

The strong outlooks from companies are showing up in Wall Street's evolving view of the quarter. While analysts now expect third-quarter earnings growth of 29.0% from S&P 500 companies, on June 1 that forecast was more than two percentage points lower.

Interestingly, the biggest change is being driven by the energy sector, where Wall Street's projected year-over-year growth surged to 128% (up from 79% in June) following a jump in crude oil prices. Tech growth estimates rose to 65%, up eight percentage points from initial estimates at the start of the quarter.

Much of the S&P 500 seems to be finding ways to offset rising costs, resulting in a higher net margin. In fact, S&P 500 net profit margins are expected to reach nearly 15% for Q3 2026, up about two percentage points from the same period last year. That would mark the index's second highest net profit margin since 2009, when FactSet began tracking the metric. Energy and tech, again, lead the expansion. Financials, meanwhile, faced the largest drag.

Analysts say some industries are better able than others to pass higher costs on to customers.

"Resilient demand, especially in manufacturing sectors, likely continued to support companies in passing through higher prices, similar as in Q2," analysts at Deutsche Bank Research wrote in a recent note. "At the same time, consumer conditions remained weak, as retail sales declined further and confidence recovered only modestly."

The earnings tailwind that's been boosting stocks could be peaking, if current estimates hold. Over the next three quarters, Wall Street sees a slowdown, with quarterly growth turning nearly flat by the second quarter of 2027.

data.title: Mergers and acquisitions
data.description:
The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 2005 GMT on Friday:

** SoftBank Group is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal in a deal that could value the US security services provider at about $18 billion, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

** Clothing retailer True Religion is exploring options, including a full sale or minority stake sale that could value the brand, known for its denim, at close to $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

** Dulux paint maker AkzoNobel and US peer Axalta Coating Systems have offered remedies in an effort to secure EU antitrust approval for their $25 billion merger, a European Commission filing showed.

** French pasta maker Panzani and Portugal's Cerealis are in exclusive talks to combine their operations in a deal valuing the merged business at about €1.8 billion ($2.03 billion), they said.

** UniCredit , Italy's second-largest bank, said the European Central Bank had authorised it to take control of Commerzbank , after a hostile takeover offer completed in July lifted its stake in the German rival to 48%.

** CCC Intelligent Solutions said it agreed to be acquired by a consortium of private investment firms led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management in a $6.1 billion take-private deal.

** Britain's culture minister Lisa Nandy said she would not refer Axel Springer's planned purchase of the Telegraph Media Group to a more detailed competition investigation, clearing the way for the deal to proceed.

** Thoma Bravo-owned cybersecurity company Proofpoint will buy data security firm Varonis Systems in an all-cash deal valued at about $6.3 billion, the companies said.

data.title: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries rise in August; China holdings drop -data
data.description:
Foreign holdings of U.S. Treasuries edged higher in August after two months of declines, data from the Treasury Department showed on Friday, led by gains in holdings from the UK and Canada.

Holdings of U.S. Treasuries rose to $9.331 trillion in August, from $9.248 trillion in the previous month. Compared with a year earlier, Treasuries owned by foreigners were up less than 1%.

China's holdings, however, dropped to $590.7 billion, the lowest since August 2008
